LESSON: FIELDWORK

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa
Topic 4.6: Fieldwork
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fieldwork, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa in Grade 7 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is fieldwork important in social studies? 2. How should we conduct fieldwork?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use digital devices to search for methods of data collection (observation, questionnaire, interview, and focus group discussion),

2. engage a resource person on the challenges including road safety concerns and possible solutions in carrying out fieldwork,

3. search online on the methods of data analysis after fieldwork,

4. use mean, median, and mode to analyse road safety data from the locality and present in class,

5. watch documentary on the value field work in investigating phenomena immediate environment and write main points. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use digital devices to search for methods of data collection (observation, questionnaire, interview, and focus group discussion),
2. engage a resource person on the challenges including road safety concerns and possible solutions in carrying out fieldwork,
3. search online on the methods of data analysis after fieldwork,
4. use mean, median, and mode to analyse road safety data from the locality and present in class,
5. watch documentary on the value field work in investigating phenomena immediate environment and write main points. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fieldwork together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking: learners value fieldwork in investigating phenomena in the immediate environment.

● Communication and Collaboration: learners brainstorm on the challenges and possible solutions in carrying out fieldwork

Values:
• Responsibility: learners demonstrate self-drive as they carry out fieldwork.

• Respect: learners show respect to the people they interact with during fieldwork

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and Security: learners carry out fieldwork and exercise caution as they investigate phenomena in the immediate

environment.

Link to other Subjects:

Learners apply listening and speaking skills as they discuss challenges likely to be encountered during field work and possible

solutions.
